title: The Rec Room League
teaser: Tonight the humans play. The dog runs the snack bar.
clue: Two sports, one living room, and a very serious spectator.
reveal: Turn a hallway into a tiny sports hall with a soft mini golf hole and a plush-pin bowling lane. You play, your dog is mascot and referee with a snack bar, and a turn is on offer whenever they like.
objective: Play a soft ball mini golf hole and a plush-pin bowling lane yourself, while your dog watches, visits the snack bar and joins in if they want.
instructions: Clear a hallway or open floor about three meters long, with grippy footing (a runner or yoga mat). Use a soft foam or fabric ball bigger than your dog's mouth, with no squeaker. Put a mat with a water bowl and a few pieces of the ration to one side, away from the lane. That is the snack bar.
Build the golf hole: lay a large laundry basket on its side against a wall as the cup, with a rolled towel to guide it in. Add a folded towel as a 'bunker' halfway.
Build the bowling lane: stand six large plush toys or rolled towels in a triangle at the far end, with a rolled towel along each side as bumpers.
Round one, golf: sit or kneel and roll the ball toward the cup, three goes. Your dog may watch, wander or sniff. Announce each shot in your best commentator voice.
Round two, bowling: roll the ball down the lane at the pins and cheer the 'strikes'. Reset the pins with a flourish.
Intermission: after each round, call the snack bar to order. Whatever your dog nibbles or sniffs there is the half-time show.
Your dog's turn (only if they are keen): roll the ball softly past them or toward the pins and let them nudge, chase or ignore it. Stop the moment they lose interest, then name the league champion.
twist: You are the athlete: your dog is the mascot, the referee and the snack bar's best customer, and gets a turn whenever they fancy it.
variations: For a seated owner: play from a chair and roll the ball a shorter distance.
For a dog who likes to run: use the yard or a long hallway and let them chase a slow, soft roll after you have bowled.
For a dog who ignores balls: skip your dog's turn and keep the snack bar.
For a puppy: use one soft ball and two large plush pins, with no stuffing coming out, and play for five minutes.
completion: You have played both rounds, your dog has visited the snack bar, and a league champion has been named.
photoIdea: Photograph the plush pins mid-tumble with your dog watching from the edge, or the snack bar with your dog's nose in it.
memoryPrompt: Who took the first strike, you or the dog?
supplies: A soft ball bigger than your dog's mouth
Six large plush toys or rolled towels
optionalSupplies: A few pieces of today's ration
substitutes: No soft ball? Use a rolled pair of socks bigger than your dog's mouth, or a large soft toy.
dietNotes: The snack bar is only a few pieces counted from the day's ration. Ask your vet about your dog's diet. For a food-free version put a toy on the mat.
safety: Use only soft, large balls and plush pins, with nothing hard or breakable in the lane.
Check the floor is grippy and clear before any chase; stop if your dog starts to slide.
Remove plush toys your dog starts to tear, and run it one dog at a time.
